newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 remains weak ahead of Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 remains weak ahead of Wall Street.

text.p: Leading UK blue chips remained depressed in thin trading on Monday in the wake of the Dow's plunge on Friday.

By 1305 GMT, the benchmark FTSE 100 was down 23.4 points to 4,247.3, off the day's worst level at 4,232.9 ahead of Wall Street's open. Trading volume was thin, with only 338.6 million shares changing hands.
Worries that interest rates are poised to rise on both sides of the Atlantic are likely to keep equity markets under pressure, dealers said.
UK blue chips inched toward the day's highs as S&P 500 futures rebounded on Globex. They were up 1.50 points to 740.05 amid a steady bond market.
"We're just waiting to see what Wall Street does next," said one dealer. "People are just staying out of the market."
Earlier, news that UK March output prices fell by 0.1 percent eased worries about inflation, although UK interest rates are generally expected to be raised soon after the May 1 election.
Yet the market's near-term direction is likely to be determined by events on Wall Street, they said.
The next indication of U.S. inflation will come on Tuesday when the U.S. government reports on March consumer prices.

"The (U.S. consumer price) figures will be important, but I don't think that's what everyone is waiting for," the dealer said. "People are just waiting until the market calms down and that might not happen until after the election."
Among individual stocks, shares in Great Universal Stores Plc bucked the weaker trend, rising 7-1/2p to 634 after SBC Warburg raised the stock to "hold" from "reduce".
PowerGen Plc gained 7-1/2p to 635-1/2, after NatWest Securities highlighted the stock's yield attractions.

Dealers said electricity stocks as a whole continued to advance from talk that the "windfall" tax on privatised utilities planned by the opposition Labour party would not be as large as previously feared.

Shares in Energy Group Plc jumped 9-1/2p to 497-1/2 on press reports that it was in the running to acquire U.S. power group New England Electric Systems, a move that would bolster its presence in the U.S., analysts said.
